subject: Post-call: HeliosCorp inference needs & next steps
messages:
From: Alex Duran <alex.d@heliosc.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: platform@heliosc.com
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2023 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today's discovery call

Thanks everyone for the time this morning. Quick recap from HeliosCorp's side so we're aligned before we dig into ops details next week:

- Use case: real-time customer support summarization + intent routing for multilingual chat.
- Current traffic: 600 reqs/min (peak 1,200 reqs/min during EMEA morning), 95th latency for full-turn is ~420ms today (we use our current LLM provider).
- Targets: want steady-state p95 <= 200ms for single-turn summarization and p95 <= 300ms for multi-turn routing.
- Model preference: open to open-weight Llama2-70B quantized or a 30B variant; accuracy on safety stems is a blocker.
- Data concerns: must not persist raw user messages outside VPC; audit trail required for compliance.

I'll attach a CSV of sampled QPS by hour. We'd like Redwood to propose a short topology + rough cost ballpark ahead of the technical deep-dive.

— Alex
Alex Duran
VP, Platform Engineering
HeliosCorp

Attachment: heliosc_prod_qps.csv (CSV, 2.1 KB)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Duran <alex.d@heliosc.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2023 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery call

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the CSV. Putting this into a concise Redwood-facing recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap of pain & goals (you covered these well):
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms single-turn, p95 <= 300ms multi-turn.
- Throughput: steady 600 rpm (10 rps), peaks to 1,200 rpm (20 rps) with burst behavior during EMEA morning.
- Privacy: VPC-only deployment, no persistent storage of raw utterances outside your environment; audit logs required.
- Model: leaning toward 30–70B open models; need evaluation on safety/accuracy.

High-level proposal (what we'll bring to the deep-dive):
1) Topology options:
   - Private deployment (VPC) with Redwood Private control plane + on-prem inference nodes or dedicated GPUs in your cloud account.
   - Hybrid setup: hosted model variants as fallback for burst periods, with routing policy to fall back to a smaller model when capacity constrained.
2) Performance levers:
   - Model choice + quantization profile (int8/llm.int4 where applicable).
   - Continuous batching with adaptive flush thresholds to hit p95 targets.
   - Prefix/KV caching for multi-turn flows to reduce repeated compute.
3) SLOs & telemetry we need from you before the deep-dive:
   - Representative traces for 200–600 token uses (sampled spans), error profile, and tail-latency distribution.
   - Any shard/region constraints (we noted EMEA morning peaks).
4) Compliance: confirm KMS/HSM preference and retention window for audit logs.

Attachments: I included a 1-page preliminary capacity sketch and a proposed agenda for the technical deep-dive.

Proposed next steps:
- Can we book a 90-minute deep-dive with your infra + ML engineer next Wednesday (Mar 29) at 10:00 AM PT? That session will cover topology tradeoffs, kernel/quant strategy, and a rough cost/latency simulation.
- If you can share 48 hours of traces and the exact safety/regulatory checklist, Rishi will pre-run a quick mapping to our quant profiles.

Looping in Rishi and Ben from Redwood to keep continuity. Rishi — can you prepare a short note with the quantization options we recommend for 30–70B variants? Ben — can you prepare a baseline capacity estimate for private VPC deployment (gpus and autoscale behavior)?

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_slo_draft.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Alex Duran <alex.d@heliosc.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 23 Mar 2023 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery call

Alex/Jasmine — quick tech addendum from my side based on the CSV and targets:

Model & quantization recommendations (short):
- 30B (FP16) or 70B (int8/llm.int4) tradeoff: 70B gives better safety/multi-turn coherence for summarization; with int8 and end-to-end kernel tuning we can often see 2–3x cost reduction vs FP16 with modest latency impact.
- For your p95 targets, I recommend testing a 30B FP16 tuned for low-latency and a 70B quantized variant in parallel (A/B) — route 80% traffic to 30B, 20% to 70B for quality checks.

Topology sketch (what I'd bring to the deep-dive):
- VPC Private control-plane + dedicated GPU pool in your cloud account (g4dn/g5 + a 3rd-party nvlink-enabled baremetal option if you want lower latencies).
- KV cache at the service tier with per-tenant TTLs to avoid persisting raw messages longer than policy.
- Smart router for region-aware routing; keep a small reserved capacity in EU region to handle morning peaks.

Capacity & latency notes:
- Based on your peak 20 rps and typical token lengths (median 120 tokens, tail 400), initial estimate is 6–8 x A100-equivalent GPUs for 70B-int8 with continuous batching and a target 150–220ms token latency path. (Ben — please refine.)

Data & compliance asks:
- Confirm whether HeliosCorp requires HSM-bound keys or standard KMS. Also confirm SLA window for log retention (30/90/365 days).

I will bring microbenchmarks for Llama2-30B / 70B quant profiles and a short kernel-selection matrix.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Applied ML — Inference Optimization
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Alex Duran <alex.d@heliosc.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 23 Mar 2023 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery call

Alex — I ran a quick back-of-envelope based on the CSV and Rishi's guidance. Notes attached are intentionally conservative.

Key points:
- Baseline for 70B-int8: 7 x A100-equivalent (or 10 x T4-like if you prefer cheaper instances) to maintain p95 <= 300ms under sustained 20 rps with ~200 token avg.
- For 30B-FP16 low-latency path: 3–4 x A100-equivalent.
- Autoscale policy suggestion: keep 20% headroom for burst-to-peak smoothing, and a small hot-pool in eu-west-1 to shave EMEA tail.
- Cost direction: hybrid (primary private fleet + hosted overflow) reduces commit spend while protecting latency SLOs.

Attachments: network_diagram.png (PNG, 78 KB)

Next step: if we confirm traces and safety checklist, we'll produce a one-pager with concrete GPU counts, estimated monthly cost ranges (hosted vs private), and a dev plan for a two-week pilot.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Duran <alex.d@heliosc.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: platform@heliosc.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 24 Mar 2023 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery call

Thanks Jasmine, Rishi, Ben — this is exactly the level of detail we were hoping for. Two quick confirmations: 
1) We'll provision a short-lived S3 bucket with sampled traces (24 hours) and a read-only IAM role for Redwood to pull them.
2) We require 90-day audit logs and HSM-backed keys for production.

We can do the 90-minute deep-dive on Wed Mar 29 at 10:00 AM PT. Invite sent. Please include your ML infra lead and a brief test plan in the invite. We'll expect the capacity one-pager before the meeting.

Alex
Alex Duran
VP, Platform Engineering, HeliosCorp
